prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-04-28. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.92 |
| Retained earnings       | -8,881M |
| Current liabilities     | 11,449M |
| Current assets          | 10,559M |
| Shareholders' equity    | -8,465M |
| Total liabilities       | 39,015M |
| Total assets            | 30,558M |
| EBIT / operating income | 777M |
| Revenue                 | 9,532M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-04-28, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported balance sheet shows severe distress: negative shareholders' equity, liabilities materially exceeding assets, and retained earnings deeply negative, all of which imply balance-sheet insolvency and a high probability of default. Liquidity is also weak (current ratio < 1), while the modest positive EBIT does not offset the structural insolvency. These metrics map to the lower end of the CCC category on the 21-grade scale.
DECISION: CCC-
